chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: It is not permissible for the one praying to pray with one prayer except with one Takbir, unless he has prayed a prayer, completed its bowing and prostration, and raised his head from it, then he repeats it.

key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةٍ: Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar), the opening declaration that initiates prayer
key_terms.رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ: He raised his head (signifying the completion of the cycle)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on restarting a prayer if a mistake is made before completing the cycle?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) clarification on the structural integrity of the *Takbirat al-Ihram*, establishing that the opening declaration anchors the prayer unit. The Imam further refines the jurisprudence of error (*khata’*) by mandating the completion of the current *ruku’* and *sujood* before restarting, thereby preserving the sequential continuity (*tartib*) essential to valid worship. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precise ritual form while accommodating human fallibility without invalidating the entire act of devotion.
